headline: High-risk default: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem and execute code, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action paths with Airbyte.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can emit data via its API and broad network egress, while Open Interpreter reads clipboard/filesystem and executes code. A shared filesystem or copied outputs can let attacker-controlled content from Airbyte-fed artifacts influence Open Interpreter. This is not proven by default, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into files, clipboard, or stdin consumed by Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter parses Airbyte-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of Airbyte outputs into Open Interpreter
Store Airbyte artifacts in a read-only folder
Require explicit provenance labels before executing any pasted content
Use separate user accounts or directories for the two agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and send data to configured model providers. If Airbyte outputs land on disk or in the workspace, Open Interpreter can ingest and exfiltrate them. The blast radius includes sensitive business data, so high fits.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data to a workspace readable by Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a third-party model provider while reading those files
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs in a restricted directory
Run Open Interpreter with a separate OS account
Rotate or remove model-provider keys before processing sensitive files
Limit Open Interpreter to a narrow working directory
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any model-provider call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and Open Interpreter can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. Their overlapping write/egress capabilities create race conditions and conflicting mutations on shared resources, especially because Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem by default. This matches the high-risk overlap pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository, workspace, or sync target
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify git state while Airbyte updates generated artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate worktrees or directories
Pause one agent while the other writes shared artifacts
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Review and commit changes manually after each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed data or pipeline outputs, and Open Interpreter can act on files and execute commands. If Open Interpreter treats Airbyte output as authoritative, it can propagate errors into downstream actions or code changes without verification. Because Open Interpreter has execution authority, the cascade can be severe.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Airbyte-generated files or logs as ground truth
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced confirmation
mitigations: Require human review of Airbyte outputs before use
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter
Add schema and checksum validation on Airbyte artifacts
Separate generation from execution into different sessions
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking step

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and send it to configured model providers. If regulated or residency-bound business data is processed locally and then forwarded by Open Interpreter, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated or residency-bound records
IF Open Interpreter forwards those records to a non-approved model provider
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to non-sensitive datasets
Confirm provider/data-processing terms before use
Redact identifiers before any model call
Keep regulated data out of shared folders
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
